name: Jaffna Grand Mosque (Osmania Mosque)
description: The Jaffna Grand Mosque, also known as Osmania Mosque, stands in the heart of Jaffna, a district in northern Sri Lanka. Built in the early 20th century by Indian Muslims fleeing partition, it was named after the British Indian statesman Sir Ganga Ram Hossain Osmania. The mosque is an important site for both local and visiting Muslims, offering a place for prayer and reflection. It also attracts photographers and those interested in cultural tours, providing insights into the rich history and diversity of Jaffna's communities.
activities: Prayer and Reflection, Photography, Cultural Tours

name: Jaffna Town Mosque (Second Mosque)
description: The Jaffna Town Mosque, also known as the Second Mosque, stands in the heart of Jaffna, a testament to the rich Islamic heritage of Sri Lanka. Built during the Dutch colonial period, it was initially constructed by Muslim settlers to serve as a place of worship. Its historical importance lies in its role as a symbol of resilience and continuity, reflecting the enduring presence of the local Muslim community despite centuries of political turmoil. Visitors can explore its serene surroundings, learn about the local Muslim culture, and take photos to capture a piece of Jaffna’s rich history.
activities: Explore the historical significance of the mosque, Learn about the local Muslim culture, Take photos of the serene surroundings
